description:
Conformance for the additional coreutils (uu_* backed) plus our own yes/seq/rev/tac.

Scripts are written so every comparison is deterministic: nondeterministic commands (mktemp,
shuf, date's wall clock) are wrapped so only a fixed-content check is printed, never raw output
that would differ between the wasm shell and the oracle even when both are "correct".

cases.name: basename: strips directory and suffix
dirname: strips the last component
realpath: resolves relative and .. components
readlink: prints a symlink target
ln: hard link shares content
ln: symlink resolves via readlink
cases.script: printf soft > /tmp/lns-target; ln -s lns-target /tmp/lns-link; readlink /tmp/lns-link; cat /tmp/lns-link

cases.name: link: creates a second directory entry for the same file
unlink: removes exactly one file
cases.script: printf x > /tmp/unlink-f; unlink /tmp/unlink-f; if test -e /tmp/unlink-f; then echo exists; else echo gone; fi

cases.name: rmdir: removes an empty directory
cases.script: mkdir /tmp/rmdir-d; rmdir /tmp/rmdir-d; if test -d /tmp/rmdir-d; then echo exists; else echo gone; fi

cases.name: mktemp: creates a fresh file and directory
cases.script: f=$(mktemp); if test -f "$f"; then echo file-ok; fi; rm -f "$f"; d=$(mktemp -d); if test -d "$d"; then echo dir-ok; fi; rmdir "$d"

cases.name: truncate: shrinks a file to an exact size
nl: numbers non-blank lines
paste: merges lines of two files column-wise
join: merges on a common sorted field
cases.script:
printf '1 a
2 b
3 c
' > /tmp/join-1; printf '1 x
2 y
4 z
' > /tmp/join-2; join /tmp/join-1 /tmp/join-2

cases.name: comm: three-column set comparison
fold: wraps at a fixed width
fmt: fills short lines into a paragraph
cases.script: printf 'one two three four five six\n' | fmt -w 10

cases.name: expand: tabs become spaces
unexpand: runs of spaces become tabs
tsort: topological order of a DAG
split: splits a file into fixed-size line chunks
cases.script:
printf '1
2
3
4
' > /tmp/split-src; cd /tmp && split -l 2 split-src split-part-; cat split-part-aa; echo ---; cat split-part-ab

cases.name: csplit: splits a file at a line number
cases.script:
printf '1
2
3
4
' > /tmp/csplit-src; cd /tmp && csplit -z csplit-src 3; cat xx00; echo ---; cat xx01

cases.name: base64: round-trips through encode and decode
cases.script: printf hello | base64; printf hello | base64 | base64 -d

cases.name: base32: encodes to the expected alphabet
basenc: base64 mode matches base64
md5sum: hashes fixed content
sha1sum: hashes fixed content
sha256sum: hashes and self-checks
cases.script: printf hello > /tmp/sha-f; sha256sum /tmp/sha-f > /tmp/sha-f.sha256; cd /tmp && sha256sum -c sha-f.sha256

cases.name: sha512sum: hashes fixed content
b2sum: hashes fixed content
cksum: checksums and counts a file
od: dumps bytes as hex with no offset column
date: formats a fixed epoch in UTC
date: +%s round-trips through -d @
cases.script: s=$(date -u -d @1700000000 +%s); if test "$s" = 1700000000; then echo ok; fi

cases.name: expr: arithmetic and string length
factor: prints the prime factorization
numfmt: reformats to human-readable IEC units
shuf: permutes without changing the multiset
yes: repeats y forever until the reader stops
yes: repeats the given words
seq: default integer range
seq: single-argument form counts from 1
seq: decimal increment
seq: descending range with a negative increment
seq: equal-width zero pads to the widest endpoint
seq: custom separator only appears between terms
seq: streams instead of materializing a huge range
rev: reverses ascii lines
rev: reverses UTF-8 characters, not bytes
rev: terminates against an endless producer
cases.script: while :; do echo x; done | rev | head -n 1

cases.name: rev: continues past a missing file without the os-error suffix
tac: reverses line order
tac: a missing final newline fuses onto the previous line
tac: unsupported regex separator refuses

stderr.text: tac: -r/--regex is unsupported in bash-tool (only a fixed-string separator is implemented)

expected.reason: bash-tool refuses tac's regex-separator mode; only a fixed-string separator is implemented

cases.name: tac: reverses several files independently in operand order
tac: reports a missing file and keeps going
yes: reports broken pipe when SIGPIPE is ignored
yes: default disposition still yields the synthetic 141 status
seq: reports broken pipe when SIGPIPE is ignored
seq: default disposition still yields the synthetic 141 status
seq: -f exponential format matches C printf
seq: -f general format strips trailing zeros
seq: invalid float argument diagnostic matches GNU
seq: zero increment diagnostic matches GNU
seq: missing operand diagnostic matches GNU
seq: extra operand diagnostic matches GNU
date: --resolution
date: -s cannot set the clock
cases.script: date -u -s @0; echo status=$?; date -u -s '2020-01-01'; echo status=$?

cases.name: sort: -c reports the first disorder
cases.script:
printf 'a
b
' | sort -c; echo status=$?; printf 'a
c
b
a
' | sort -c; echo status=$?; printf 'a
a
' | sort -cu; echo status=$?; sort -c /dev/null; echo status=$?; printf 'x 2
y 10
' | sort -c -k2n; echo status=$?

cases.name: sort: -C is silent
cases.script:
printf 'b
a
' | sort -C; echo status=$?; printf 'a
b
' | sort -C; echo status=$?

cases.name: sort: -m merges sorted inputs
cases.script:
printf '1
3
5
' >/tmp/a; printf '2
3
4
' >/tmp/b; printf '' >/tmp/e; sort -m /tmp/a /tmp/b /tmp/e; echo status=$?; sort -mu /tmp/a /tmp/b; echo status=$?; printf '5
3
1
' >/tmp/c; sort -m -nr /tmp/c - <<<$'4
2'; echo status=$?
